lines.text: Three short. Three long. Three short.
And I knew *exactly* what it meant.
I wrote it down.
Dot, dot, dot. S.
Dash, dash, dash. O.
Dot, dot, dot. S.
S. O. S.
Someone on the other side of that hatch was asking for *help.*
Rule one. Never open Hatch 3. Not for anyone. Not even for me.
If I opened it, and there really was no air, the station would empty in seconds.
And so would I.
My hand was on the wheel.
I let go.
The knocks came every night. For nine nights.
I told myself it was a trick. I didn't believe it.
Day seventy. No knocks.
Day seventy-one. Nothing.
Day seventy-two. Nothing.
Whoever it was had stopped asking.
Or had stopped being able to.
But every morning, the tank still lost 1.7 kilos.
They'd stopped knocking. They hadn't stopped *breathing.*
Day eighty-eight.
I decided to check the one thing that told me there was no air.
The gauge.
Four screws. I took it off the wall.
A pressure gauge needs a sensor on the other side of the wall, and a wire that brings the number to you.
So I followed the wire with my flashlight.
Past the brackets. Past the insulation. Toward Module 3.
The wire went into the wall.
And stopped.
The gauge was never connected to *anything.*
